fieldsChanged.before: In congenital diaphragmatic hernia (CDH) bag-and-mask ventilation pushes air into the stomach/bowel, which then expands inside the chest and compresses the lung further. The baby should be intubated immediately, so (c) is the incorrect statement.
fieldsChanged.after: In suspected congenital diaphragmatic hernia, avoid bag-mask ventilation because it can insufflate the stomach and bowel, worsening intrathoracic compression; establish the airway with endotracheal intubation and decompress the stomach. Current neonatal resuscitation prioritizes effective ventilation; chest compressions are used when the heart rate remains below 60/min despite adequate ventilation, and epinephrine is considered if the rate remains below 60/min after coordinated compressions. Sodium bicarbonate is not routinely recommended during initial resuscitation. Naloxone is not an initial-resuscitation intervention and must not delay ventilation. Volume expansion is considered when blood loss is suspected and the infant remains unresponsive to resuscitation.

entries.why: Updated neonatal resuscitation wording and explanation to align with current resuscitation guidance.

fieldsChanged.after:
In a child with suspected hereditary spherocytosis, which initial investigation is most useful for assessing red-cell morphology?
Scenario: Ayoub, 5 years old, presented with pallor and jaundice. On examination he was well, jaundiced, with splenomegaly 3 cm below the costal margin, no hepatomegaly or lymphadenopathy. Hb 8 g/dL, WBC 11,000/µL, platelets 300 × 10^3/µL, MCV 87 fL and reticulocytes 15%.

fieldsChanged.before: In suspected hereditary spherocytosis, the blood film shows spherocytes and the next tests are the direct Coombs test (to exclude autoimmune haemolysis), osmotic fragility/eosin-5-maleimide binding. Haemoglobin electrophoresis is not useful here.
fieldsChanged.after: A peripheral blood film is the initial test that assesses red-cell morphology and may show spherocytes. A direct antiglobulin (Coombs) test is also important to distinguish hereditary spherocytosis from autoimmune haemolysis, but it answers a different diagnostic question. If the film and clinical picture support hereditary spherocytosis, confirmatory testing may include eosin-5-maleimide binding or other validated membrane tests.

entries.why: Clarified that the question asks for the initial investigation of red-cell morphology. A blood film answers that specific question; Coombs testing addresses autoimmune haemolysis.

fieldsChanged.before: Reticulocytes are immature, slightly larger red cells containing residual RNA (polychromasia). Reticulocytosis occurs with haemolysis (e.g. hereditary spherocytosis).

entries.why: Corrected the G6PD distractor: young red cells and reticulocytes can have higher G6PD activity than mature red cells. This leaves untreated iron-deficiency reticulocytosis as the exception.

fieldsChanged.before: Why correct: Immunoglobulin (antibody) abnormalities are mainly B-cell defects (failure of B-cell maturation, e.g. BTK mutation in X-linked agammaglobulinaemia), not T-cell failure.

entries.why: Replaced the inaccurate claim that X-linked agammaglobulinaemia is the most common abnormality with the more accurate broad category statement: antibody/B-cell deficiencies are the largest group.

Appropriate initial screening includes at least two 24-hour urinary free cortisol measurements, two late-night salivary cortisol measurements, or a 1-mg overnight dexamethasone suppression test, selected according to the clinical setting. A random serum cortisol level is not an adequate screening test.

fieldsChanged.before: Hyperglycemia draws water into the vascular space and dilutes sodium (Na falls ~1.6 mmol/l per 100 mg/dl glucose above normal) = pseudo-hyponatremia. DKA usually shows HYPERlipidemia (not low cholesterol); magnesium and calcium are not characteristically low on presentation.
fieldsChanged.after: Hyperglycaemia raises extracellular tonicity and shifts water from the intracellular to extracellular space, lowering the measured serum sodium concentration. This is translocational (hypertonic) hyponatraemia, not pseudohyponatraemia. Pseudohyponatraemia is a measurement artefact associated with markedly elevated lipids or proteins when indirect ion-selective electrode methods are used.
